pending_qa.q: What factors contributed to Vanell's decision to accept acquisition by Strabag despite a decade on the stock exchange?
pending_qa.r: Vanell stated that the level of cost and resource required to maintain its stock market listing on the Alternative Investment Market since 2016 was excessive for the size of the group and detrimental to its performance and focus. Additionally, the board believed the share price was unlikely to reflect the fundamental value of the business given illiquid trading and subdued investor sentiment towards smaller UK-quoted companies.

pending_qa.q: What was the primary reason Vanell's board cited for accepting Strabag's acquisition offer?
pending_qa.r: The first reason listed by Vanell's board was the opportunity for shareholders, including managers who own stock, to realize their entire shareholding in full at an attractive value, which the board believed delivered the value of its standalone growth strategy on an accelerated basis—essentially, shareholder cash-out was the leading motivation stated.

pending_qa.q: How long have David Taylor and Phil Bishop been hosting the Reconstruction podcast, and why is episode 200 their final episode?
pending_qa.r: David Taylor and Phil Bishop started Reconstruction in January 2020 and have been hosting for almost exactly six years. Episode 200 marks the end of the podcast with Bishop and Taylor, as both are retiring from construction journalism. Taylor is ending his role at Construction Index, and Bishop is also stepping down after this episode.

pending_qa.q: What was David Taylor's career entry point into construction journalism and what conditions prevailed in the publishing industry at that time?
pending_qa.r: David Taylor joined New Civil Engineer magazine in 1987 during the boom times for civil engineering. The magazine was owned by the Institution of Civil Engineers through Thomas Telford Publishing, and the publishing arm had to return a percentage of profits to the institution, so managers were investing heavily in the magazine with first-class travel and frequent client entertainment, including expectations to wine and dine industry figures.

pending_qa.q: How did Phil Bishop begin his career in construction journalism and what was his initial role?
pending_qa.r: Phil Bishop joined Cranes Today in 1986 as an editorial assistant. When the assistant editor left after a year and then the editor left a year later, United Trade Press promoted him from within to become editor of the magazine, a role for which he had no prior experience.

pending_qa.q: Who is succeeding David Taylor and Phil Bishop at Construction Index, and what is his background?
pending_qa.r: Will North is the successor and will be doing both the daily online news service and the magazine. He is another former editor of Cranes Today—editing it long after both Taylor and Bishop had left—and is more recently known to listeners through the Engineering Matters podcast, bringing impeccable journalism pedigree to the role.
